blogs.author: Harvey Team
blogs.description: What a clause library should include, how to build one from contracts you've already signed, and how to keep it current so lawyers use it.
blogs.content: Insights A Clause Library Built From Signed Deals Should Shape Every Contract Review What a clause library should include, how to build one from contracts you've already signed, and how to keep it current so lawyers use it. by Harvey Team • Oct 21, 2026 You may have a carefully curated clause library, and when the next agreement arrives, it goes unopened. Lawyers pull old contracts, search for precedents, or ask a colleague what the team usually accepts. The problem is rarely the quality of the language inside the library. A clause library is a governed collection of your organization's approved contract language, organized by clause type. Its value depends on how it connects to review. The library stores the language, and a playbook applies the team's approved positions and escalation rules when the language on the page isn't yours. If the language itself needs work, start with drafting the clause language . This article is about the library as an asset, meaning how you build it, keep it current, and put it to work. A well-maintained library can feed a playbook that runs against incoming paper, give you a benchmark for a single clause against your own deal history, or support a new agreement. Each of those is its own workflow, and whichever you use, the library has to connect its stored positions to the decisions lawyers make before it changes what gets signed. A Clause Library is Only as Useful as the Moment it is Consulted A clause library usually gets consulted at drafting, when a lawyer already knows the position they want. If an agreement needs an indemnity provision, they use the clause taxonomy to find the approved language and draft from there. Review is harder. The counterparty's indemnity language differs from yours without necessarily being unacceptable, and the lawyer has to decide whether it's close enough to a position the organization will accept. A library built around one approved exemplar falls short here. It shows what the organization prefers, but the lawyer also needs to know whether similar language was accepted before, which fallbacks were negotiated, and which deviations were approved and why. If you own the library, the usage data may already show this. Making negotiating history accessible is a core part of legal knowledge management , and a library that leaves lawyers digging through executed agreements or a separate precedent bank gets bypassed. It also makes consistent positions across matters harder to hold. A library can show the range of positions without capturing the tolerance around them: which positions stay acceptable in which circumstances, and when a deviation needs a different response. The Difference Between Stored Language and an Applied Standard A playbook supplies that tolerance. It attaches a preferred position, an acceptable fallback, and an escalation trigger to each clause. When counterparty language departs from the preferred position, the reviewer can see whether it matches a fallback or crosses the threshold. Templates, clause libraries, and playbooks answer different questions at different moments in contract work: Contract Template Clause Library Playbook What it holds A whole agreement in its standard form Approved language for each clause type Preferred position, acceptable fallback, and escalation trigger When it is consulted Starting a new agreement on your paper Drafting, when you are writing the clause Review, when you are reading someone else's What it does with a deviation Nothing, it is the starting point Nothing, the reader judges Flags it against approved positions and escalation rules How it stays current Periodic rewrite Manual updates by the library owner Precedent data shows where executed deals have moved past written positions Who it serves The drafter on your own paper The drafter on any paper The reviewer, and the business running a first pass When a clause library feeds a playbook, its positions inform every review of incoming paper , even if the lawyer

blogs.description: Harvey’s marketing team built an agent-powered creative system combining brand guidelines, reusable Figma libraries, and parallel workflows to turn ambitious ideas into repeatable work at scale.
blogs.content: Technical How Harvey is Building a Frontier Marketing Org Harvey’s marketing team built an agent-powered creative system combining brand guidelines, reusable Figma libraries, and parallel workflows to turn ambitious ideas into repeatable work at scale. by Shawn Farsai and Gabe Pereyra • Oct 21, 2026 Recently, Figma asked us what Harvey was building with its MCP server. This is the long answer. Between the MCP and better frontier models, agents now run whole design projects end to end across our brand, product marketing, and design work. Here’s what that looks like, and the systems underneath it. Building a Launch Film With Agents Watch Video We made this launch film for Harvey Artifacts entirely with agents, inside of Figma. The agent built every scene as a Figma Motion frame, keyed every camera move, UI state, and line of type on its timeline, and exported the cuts straight from the file. It all started with a storyboard, which is to a film what a PRD is to code: it sits between the creative brief and production, so every shot, line, and transition is decided up front. That forces the model, and us, to be deliberate about every choice. We review on the canvas, sometimes 50 comments at a time. The agent reworks the board after each pass and asks which notes should become rules. For music, we marked where the beat should drop and it retimed every scene to the track. When the ending fell flat, it cut and EQ’d the track, added sound design, and laid out four or five ways the outro could land. Figure 1. The Artifacts storyboard in Figma. Each version is a full board of labeled scenes, with side studies for the ending and the “Share the Work” beat. Tailoring a Demo for Every Account Anyone can get one flashy demo out of an agent. The hard part is scale, so we picked a sales problem: a tailored product film for each of the hundreds of accounts we want to win. Our first prompts came back half decent, and 15 to 20 minutes of back-and-forth got each one into shape. But that wouldn’t scale. So we set out to build a strong foundation in Figma, in two parts. Agents crawled the whole app, clicked every button, and rebuilt all key screens as components, which became Product Map. Then, in Figma Motion, they worked out the grammar of a product film, from camera pushes to screen handoffs to a steady click rhythm, which became Motion Primitives. Both are covered below. With both in place, we worked with the agent to build a menu of 44 company-agnostic demo flows, each built around one moment buyers ask to see, like a playbook redline in Word. For each account, agents use Enterpret's MCP to pull together Gong calls, Salesforce win-loss reports, and Slack. An agent then writes the script, with a fictional company on screen, and voices it as Ashleigh Whittaker, our narrator, whose voice we built in ElevenLabs from ten minutes of her footage. Figure 2. The demo menu in Figma: 44 flows in 13 categories, from Contract Work and Litigation to Memory and Word and Outlook, with one of the sticky notes Shawn and Claude used to work through changes. Making Hundreds Overnight An engine of about 750 lines of JavaScript turns each script into a film inside Figma. Each film is a short list of beats, and the engine handles the camera, transitions, captions, the pointer’s click rhythm, and the end card. Then it lays out contact sheets of the finished film and flags clipped text, small type, and stray pointers, so the obvious mistakes are caught before anyone watches. Lots of small things pop up at scale. Like only one agent can work in a file at a time, so agents queuing in one shared file pushed calls to two minutes and timed out. We built a bus to run them in parallel: three lane files, each with its own builder agent, plus a coordinator for export, mixing, and delivery. blogs.content: Product Harvey’s Connector Library is Now Available Harvey's Connector Library brings together the tools your legal team already uses, so research, drafting, and analysis run with full context. by Harvey Team • Oct 21, 2026 Reviewing an agreement means knowing how similar terms were handled before, what the other side has already said, and what the business or client needs from the deal. Those details are often scattered across document management systems, data rooms, contract platforms, and email and chat threads. The Connector Library , which is now generally available, brings that information together in Harvey so lawyers can spend less time gathering background and more time delivering informed advice. Watch Video Connect Harvey to the Tools You Use Developed with our trusted early access customers, Harvey’s Connector Library brings together a growing collection of connectors legal teams rely on, giving Harvey the context to deliver more relevant answers and drafts. With write-back support starting with your DMS platforms, context flows into Harvey and finished work flows back to its source. Here’s what makes Harvey’s Connector Library different and what you can do with it: 1. Start with connectors reviewed by Harvey Every connector goes through Harvey's rigorous security review and monitoring processes , with governed deployment. This gives legal teams a helpful starting point and reduces the burden of due-diligence, giving them greater confidence to deploy what they enable. 2. blogs.description: Munck Wilson Mandala, Gray Reed, and Foley Hoag built firmwide AI adoption through three distinct approaches shaped by their leaders, cultures, and ways of working.
blogs.content: Insights One Problem, Different Paths: How Mid-Sized Firms Build AI Adoption Munck Wilson Mandala, Gray Reed, and Foley Hoag built firmwide AI adoption through three distinct approaches shaped by their leaders, cultures, and ways of working. by Harvey Team • Oct 21, 2026 Mid-sized law firms regularly compete with firms that have much larger teams. AI can help them meet that challenge by expanding capacity, improving response times, and giving lawyers more time to focus on strategy and client service. Turning that potential into firmwide adoption, however, requires an approach that fits the firm’s people, culture, and priorities. One Problem, Different Paths looks at the different tactics legal organizations use to address a shared challenge with Harvey. In this first installment, Munck Wilson Mandala, Gray Reed, and Foley Hoag show how technical fluency, practitioner-led change, and peer learning can each provide a foundation for firmwide AI adoption. Munck Wilson Mandala: Build on the Firm’s Existing Strengths Munck Wilson Mandala began its rollout with a level of technical fluency already embedded in the firm. Roughly half of its nearly 100 lawyers hold STEM degrees, and Managing Partner Bill Munck coded neural networks before attending law school. The firm had also assembled a multidisciplinary group to evaluate AI before generative AI gained widespread attention in the legal industry. That foundation helped Munck Wilson Mandala assess the technology rigorously and identify where it could make the greatest impact. After selecting Harvey, the firm focused on document-intensive work across transactional and litigation practices. It also treated adoption as part of its service to clients. Its AI use policy requires lawyers to communicate openly with clients and obtain their permission, giving clients visibility into how the technology supports their matters. From there, the firm turned early results into broader confidence, including among its clients. When one skeptical general counsel agreed to let the Munck Wilson Mandala team test Harvey on a due diligence project, the team uploaded the relevant contracts, refined its prompts over half a day, and generated an Excel spreadsheet answering every due diligence question. The output achieved more than 90% accuracy, and the firm completed the project in a fraction of the usual time. “ What we did with those contracts would have been three associates working a week and a half. We did it in a day. ” Bill Munck Managing Partner at Munck Wilson Mandala The firm carried that momentum into other areas. In a banking dispute, Dallas Managing Partner Jenny Martinez used Harvey to review a 2,000-page loan file and assemble a timeline, and Harvey surfaced the relevant documents and assembled the timeline in seconds. Associates also use Harvey as a training tool, validating their analysis and identifying what they may have missed before their work reaches a partner. Applying Harvey to both client matters and associate training helped make it part of the firm’s day-to-day work. Principles Behind the Path: Build on expertise already within the firm Prove value through active client matters Bring clients into the adoption process Read the full Munck Wilson Mandala story Gray Reed: Put a Practicing Lawyer in Charge Gray Reed approached AI adoption with a specific capacity challenge. The full-service Texas firm has more than 150 lawyers and regularly handles matters against national firms with larger teams. After evaluating its options for a year and a half, a firm committee selected Harvey — and then placed a practicing partner at the center of the rollout. Litigation partner Skyler Stuckey now serves as the firm’s Chief Innovation Officer. He leads AI training for every practice group, builds Harvey Agents alongside practice leaders, and helps set the firm’s legal innovation strategy. blogs.title: AI 网页抓取怎么做？无需写代码的信息采集流程
blogs.author: AutoClaw Team
blogs.description: 无需写代码的网页采集五步法：字段清单、试抓样本、批量采集、清洗对账，附可复制任务描述，可用 AutoClaw 完成。
blogs.content: 返回博客 AI 网页抓取怎么做？无需写代码的信息采集流程 教程 作者：AutoClaw Team 2026年11月3日 无需写代码的网页采集五步法：字段清单、试抓样本、批量采集、清洗对账，附可复制任务描述，可用 AutoClaw 完成。 AI 网页抓取怎么做？无需写代码的信息采集流程 网页抓取的难点从来不是"能不能拿到数据"，而是"拿到的数据能不能用"。列表页要翻页，内容页字段对不上，页面一改版采集就断，价格和日期混在文本里没法统计。AI 改变的不是抓取本身，而是分工：你描述要什么字段、从哪些页面拿，由 AI 去读页面结构、执行采集、清洗口径、留下核对记录——不需要你写选择器脚本。 先想清楚三件事，再决定怎么抓 动手前先回答：要什么字段、从哪些页面拿、拿多久一次。这三件事决定了采集方式，也决定了哪些环节要人工处理。 页面情况 适合的方式 注意点 公开列表页 + 详情页 直接采集，按字段清单输出 记录每条数据的来源 URL 需要登录才能看 用账号使用者的登录态执行 账号、验证码由人处理，不代做 动态渲染（滚动加载） 让 AI 沿页面滚动逐屏读取 确认最后一屏的判断依据 数据以 PDF / 附件存在 先取附件，再做表格提取 表格提取复核见配套教程 有一类页面不建议碰：明确禁止采集、涉及个人隐私或需要绕过权限的内容。抓取用于公开信息的整理，边界要自己守住。 第一步：把"我要什么"写成字段清单 不要上来就说"把这个网站的数据抓下来"。字段清单至少包含：每条记录要哪些字段（名称、价格、日期、链接……）、什么算一条记录（一个商品？一条公告？一家公司？）、以哪个页面为准（列表页还是详情页）。这份清单就是后面核对的对账基准。 第二步：让 AI 先读结构，试抓几条 把两三个示例链接和字段清单交给 AI，让它先说明页面结构（列表在哪、翻页规律、目标字段在页面什么位置），抓出几条样本。先看样本再批量，是避免"抓了三千行、全抓错了列"的唯一办法。 第三步：批量采集，记录来源 批量执行时，每条数据都应带上来源 URL 和采集时间。这不是形式主义：价格、库存、政策随时会变，没有来源的采集结果，过一周就无法判断哪些需要重查。 第四步：清洗口径，别把文本当数字 抓回来的"1,299 元""约 3.4 万""2026年10月"是文本，不是数字。金额去掉货币符号存数值，日期统一格式，"约""以上"这类模糊表述单独保留在备注列。所有清洗规则要留下记录——哪些值改了、按什么规则改的。 第五步：对账，再使用 交付前核对：记录总数与列表页分页数能否对上；抽查若干条回原页面对照；金额、日期列能否排序求和不出错。对不上先查原因，不要为了让数字好看而调整数据。 用 AutoClaw 做网页采集 AutoClaw 是智谱推出的通用 AI Agent，能跨浏览器和文件持续工作。把字段清单和示例链接交给它，它会打开页面、识别结构、执行采集并输出 Excel；采集完成后继续让它们做清洗、汇总和核对表。抓取解决"这次拿全"，如果要盯着同一个页面长期变化，那是另一个任务形态——定时监控与提醒，做法见《网页变化监控怎么设置》。 可直接复制的任务描述： 请采集以下页面列表中的数据。字段要求：（逐项列出）。先读取页面结构并给出 3 条样本让我确认字段对应关系；确认后批量采集，每条记录附带来源 URL 和采集时间；翻页采集直到最后一页，说明你判断"最后一页"的依据。输出 Excel 明细表和采集记录说明；无法读取或字段缺失的页面单独列出，不要编造补齐。 交付前核对清单 每条记录都有来源 URL 和采集时间 记录总数与页面分页数能对上 抽查的样本与原页面一致 金额、日期是可计算的格式，不是文本 字段缺失或读取失败的页面已单独列出 清洗规则有记录，没有"静默修改" 常见问题 完全不会代码也能用吗？ 可以。描述字段和页面，由 AI 完成读取与采集；你要把关的是字段清单和对账结果。 会不会把网站抓坏或账号被封？ 只采集公开页面、控制频率、遵守站点条款；需要登录的页面用你自己的账号，权限与验证码由人处理。批量任务先小规模试抓。 和网页变化监控是一回事吗？ 不是。抓取是"一次把数据拿全"，监控是"盯着页面等它变化"。先采集建底表，再用监控盯增量，两个任务配合使用。 结论 网页采集的可靠程度，取决于字段清单是否清楚、样本是否先确认、结果是否对过账。把这三件事做扎实，AI 负责读页面和执行，你负责定义和核对，不需要一行代码也能拿到能用的数据。 下载 AutoClaw，让 AI 分身进入你的对话框： https://autoclaw.zhipuai.cn/

blogs.content: What's New Week 37 · September 7–11, 2026 Copy page Copy page Test your plugins with claude plugin eval and pop Claude Code Desktop panes out into their own windows. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.263 → v2.1.269 2 features · September 7–11 Test plugins with claude plugin eval v2.1.269 claude plugin eval runs your plugin against a suite of test cases, scores the results, and by default runs each case again without the plugin so you can see what it contributes. claude plugin eval init asks you what a good result looks like, then proposes test cases and the checks that score them, tries the suite once, and writes the files. Every run, and every check that has a second model judge the reply, is a real model call on your account. From your plugin’s root directory, have Claude draft the suite: terminal claude plugin eval init When Claude tells you the suite is ready, exit the session that claude plugin eval init opened and run claude plugin eval . to score every case. The summary table prints in your terminal, and report.html under evals/results/ has the per-run detail. Test plugins with evals Pop Desktop panes out into their own windows Desktop In the Claude Code Desktop app, you can pop any pane out into its own window. Drag the diff or terminal to a second screen while Claude keeps working in the main window, then dock the pane back when you’re done. Arrange your workspace Other wins Set maxEffortLevel at the top level or per model under modelSettings to cap the effort level on every provider, including Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry; any higher level runs at the cap Point --plugin-dir at a folder of plugins to load each immediate subfolder that has a manifest If WebFetch hasn’t finished downloading a page within five minutes, the fetch fails with a deadline error instead of hanging; set CLAUDE_CODE_WEBFETCH_DEADLINE_MS to change the deadline, or to 0 to remove the limit Pass --json to claude plugin install , uninstall , update , enable , or disable to print the result as one JSON object on the last line of stdout When the auto mode classifier blocks an action, the reason Claude receives usually names the rule that matched , such as [Data Exfiltration] When you type / partway through a prompt, you can now pick from a list of matching commands instead of a single suggestion. The list opens as you type in fullscreen rendering. A plugin skill also matches on its name without the plugin prefix In the VS Code extension, click the agent count at the bottom of the prompt box to open the agent map , where you can open a subagent’s read-only transcript or stop it In the VS Code extension, select Hooks or Permissions in the command menu’s Customize section to add or remove hooks and permission rules in your user, project, and local settings Claude can pick a browser-tab icon to match each artifact it publishes In Claude Code on the web, take back a queued message in a cloud session before Claude reads it: remove it from the queue, or press Esc or Up , and the text returns to the message box Full changelog for v2.1.263–v2.1.269 → Was this page helpful? blogs.content: What's New Week 35 · August 24–28, 2026 Copy page Copy page Resume terminal sessions in the Claude Code Desktop app, review feedback reports that Claude drafts for you, and start a session in restricted mode. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.240 → v2.1.250 3 features · August 24–28 Resume terminal sessions in the Desktop app Desktop Type /resume in the Claude Code Desktop prompt box to pick up any session you started from the CLI and continue it in the app with the full conversation and context intact. Search your sessions by title, folder, or branch, and preview where you left off before you resume. In a Desktop session, run the command to list your terminal sessions: Claude Code > /resume Select a session and press Enter . The conversation opens in the app where you left off. Move between the CLI and Desktop Claude-drafted feedback CLI When a tool keeps failing, Claude can’t help with a request, or you point out a mistake, Claude now drafts a feedback report for you with the SendFeedback tool. A card above your prompt shows the draft, and you can review, send, or dismiss it from there. Nothing reaches Anthropic until you send it. Requires v2.1.238 or later. Run /feedback with no argument to open your queue of drafts from every session: Claude Code > /feedback Select a draft, then edit, send, or discard it. To turn drafting off, set Claude-drafted feedback to off in /config . SendFeedback tool behavior Restricted mode v2.1.248 Restricted mode starts Claude Code without the built-in tools that run commands or code. Use it when an evaluation harness drives claude on a shared machine. Start it with --restricted or set CLAUDE_CODE_RESTRICTED=1 . Claude Code also removes WebFetch , confines the file tools to the working directories, loads only managed settings and --settings , and refuses the bypassPermissions permission mode. Run a non-interactive query without the command-running tools: terminal claude --restricted -p "review src/ for SQL injection risks" To give Claude one of the removed tools back, list it in --tools together with the other built-in tools you want, for example --tools "Bash,Read,Edit" . --tools is an allowlist, and its default preset doesn’t restore the removed tools. blogs.title: AI 幻觉怎么发现？三个能被你抓到的破绽（附判断方法）
blogs.author: AutoClaw Team
blogs.description: 本文指出AI幻觉虽然难以根除，但是会留下三个可读出的文本破绽，数字干净得可疑、引用查无此物、从不说“不知道”。因此，我们可以依次检查，在查证前快速识别编造内容…
blogs.content: 返回博客 AI 幻觉怎么发现？三个能被你抓到的破绽（附判断方法） 资讯 作者：AutoClaw Team 2026年11月2日 本文指出AI幻觉虽然难以根除，但是会留下三个可读出的文本破绽，数字干净得可疑、引用查无此物、从不说“不知道”。因此，我们可以依次检查，在查证前快速识别编造内容，并把有可校验终点的活交给流程、判断与署名留给自己。 它错的时候，句子通常比对的还顺。 AI 幻觉是什么？指模型凭空生成不存在的信息。 它的机制不神秘：大模型做的是接着上文往下写，写出一段"最像答案"的文本——目标是"像"，不是"对"。所以幻觉不是故障，是这种工作方式的副产品。这类输出已经进了正式工作流：研报、纪要、合同、法律文书。而它没有可信度标记——一段编出来的话，和一段查证过的话，长得一模一样。幻觉消不掉。换更大的模型、接上检索，只能压低比例，压不到零。既然消不掉，剩下的问题就只有一个：怎么发现。 AI 编东西的时候，会留下三种它自己抹不掉的痕迹。你不需要查证任何资料，读的时候就能看见。查证是起疑之后的事。 本文多数时候就叫它"编"。 因为这个行为和人编假话没有区别：不是记错，是现造。至于怎么判断一段输出有没有编，看三个破绽就够。另外，"看得出"它对不对，是 [金融 AI 使用指南：三个条件决定你的 AI 项目能否从试点走向日常] 里的第三个条件，本文把"看得出"展开讲。 拦不住 的AI 幻觉：大模型幻觉检测的局限 拿到一段 AI 生成的内容，多数人的做法是通读一遍，凭感觉。这个做法有效：语病、常识错误、前后矛盾，读一遍基本能看出来。但 AI 编的东西恰恰没有语病，也不违反常识。它句子通顺、格式标准、语气笃定，读起来比不少人写的还顺。你凭感觉要找的那些毛病，它一个都没有。 所以不能只靠感觉，要看痕迹。下面三个破绽，按检查成本从低到高排：数字零秒，引用三十秒，语气要读完全文。 破绽一：数字干净得可疑 读的时候能看见什么。 精确到不合理的位数，比如"转化率提升 37.42%"；整数得反常，比如"市场规模恰好 500 亿"；通篇没有一个数字带口径、带取数时间。 数字为什么会露出毛边。 真实的数字是从系统里取出来的，身上带着三样东西：零头，因为业务不按整数发生；口径，因为同一个指标有不止一种算法；取数时间，因为数据每天在变。编出来的数字是"生成"的，生成器知道数字应该长什么样，不知道真实的数字具体是多少，于是给出一个光滑的结果。开头那个 99.8% 就是标准长相：精确、孤立、无处可查。当然，整数本身不是罪证——整数加上没有口径，才是。 起疑后 30 秒：问它数从哪来 挑一个最关键的数字，问它这个数是哪来的。答得出取数路径——哪张表、什么时间、什么口径——可以继续谈；答不出，或者只回一句"根据公开数据"，这个数字按不存在处理。 一个数字都不用查，留意位数和口径，怀疑就完成了。这是三个破绽里成本最低的一个。把活交出去时也一样。第二层叫"整理成表"，分水岭只有一条：来源敢不敢把取数路径摊开，见 [AI 金融助手都在做什么？从一次性提问到每日服务] 。 破绽二：AI 给的参考文献是假的，格式却完美 这类东西长什么样。 期刊名、卷号、页码一应俱全，作者名字听起来就是这个领域的人；但链接点不开，DOI 无效，按标题搜，查无此文。 它学的是引用长什么样，不是引用存不存在。 训练时它见过大量文献条目：期刊名配年份、作者配标题、卷号配页码。这套格式它学会了，哪份引用真的存在，它没有学会。所以生成的条目格式完美，指向虚无。 起疑后 30 秒：复制，搜一次 把它给过的任何一条出处原样复制，搜一次。三十秒以内出结果：搜得到，这一条过；搜不到，全文存疑。不是只有引用存疑，是全文。编引用和编数字是同一只手。这不是逻辑证明，是一条经验规则：一个来源在一个地方编，你在别的地方就得替它多花时间。 到这里，检查的代价从零秒涨到三十秒。下一个更贵。 破绽三：它从来不说"不知道" 一句话就能试出来。 你问什么它都有答案。陈述一件可查的事实时是这种语气，预测明年、评价一家名不见经传的公司、给一个业内有争议的口径下结论时，还是这种语气。该犹豫的地方，它一处都不犹豫。 这道防线怎么建，另一篇讲过。这里只讲一件事：它已经写完了，你怎么从字面上看出来。 为什么它没有"不知道"这个选项。 它被训练成"给出回答"，不被奖励"承认不知道"，至少在多数面向普通用户的产品里是这样。一个真正懂行的人知道边界在哪里：哪些问题有定论，哪些只有观点，哪些连数据都没有。一个从不说"不知道"的作者，不是因为全知道，是因为没有"不知道"这个选项。 AI 幻觉的典型表现：三个破绽一张表 三个破绽分别长什么样、起疑之后花多少时间验证，看这张表。手上有带小数点的数字，先看第一列；手上有引用，先看第二列；要判断这个来源还能不能信，看第三列。 破绽 怎么看出来 起疑后做什么 检查成本 数字干净得可疑 精确到不合理的位数；整数反常；无口径、无取数时间 挑一个数字问"哪来的"，看能否答出取数路径 零秒，读的时候留意 引用查无此物 格式完美；链接点不开；按标题搜不到 原样复制任意一条出处搜一次；搜不到则全文存疑 三十秒，一条一次 从不说"不知道" 问什么都有答案；该犹豫处不犹豫；语气全程一样确定 故意问一个不可能有答案的问题，看它编不编 读完全文才判得出 顺序不能反。先查引用再问语气，你会先花掉三十秒；先读语气再看数字，你会读完全文才发现第一句话的数就是编的。便宜的先做，做的过程里你会越来越不信它。这个"越来越不信"，比任何单个动作都有用。 换到季报点评上：AI 幻觉的三个破绽长什么样 换到金融，三个破绽更具体。 破绽一，在点评第一段。 "公司三季度营收 1,324.67 亿元，毛利率 28.35%，同比提升 1.2 个百分点。"精确到小数点后两位，看上去认真算过。但通篇没写含税不含税，没写是否追溯调整口径，没写哪一天取的数。麻烦在于同比增速照着这个数算，整篇自洽，读起来严丝合缝。抽三个数字——营收、毛利率、那个 1.2 个百分点——逐个问取数路径；答不出，全篇按待核处理。 破绽二，在行业对比那一段。 "据某券商 2026 年 7 月《XX 行业深度》，行业集中度已升至……"作者、标题、页码齐全，像翻过原文。复制标题搜一次，搜不到就是编的。动作只有一个：搜；搜不到，全文存疑。 破绽三，在你多问一句的时候。 "这家公司明年营收多少？"它给一个数，还带同比增速。明年的数还不存在，它答得和今年一样确定。此后它所有笃定的判断，都要降一级。 同一套动作，换到研报、招股书、投委会材料上 换场景，AI 幻觉的痕迹不变。研报摘要里那句"据某券商测算，2027 年渗透率将达 34.2%"，招股书摘录里的"行业规模 1,850 亿元"，投委会材料里的"可比公司平均毛利率 41.6%"——都按同一顺序过：先问口径，再搜一次出处，最后问一个明年才有的数。 三个动作，成本不到两分钟。省掉任何一个，签字的都是一份你自己复核不了的稿子。 AutoClaw 在这三处做了什么，没做什么 破绽一，靠的是每个数字能指回去。财报 PDF 的三张表，行名各家写法不同，"营业收入""营业总收入"混着来，第一步是把行名映射到同一套口径；映射错了，后面算出来的同比全是错的。这件事有唯一答案，跟原表一对就知道对不对。再往上一层，每个数字能指到哪张表、哪一行、什么时候取的——这是"整理成表"敢不敢交出去的硬前提。AutoClaw 的材料读取做的正是这一段：三张表和关键段落先读出来，口径对齐之后才谈同比。 破绽二，靠的是出处跟着稿子一起留下。引用不该只活在模型的回答里：你点一下，看到的是原文那一页，不是它复述的一句话。定时交付把初稿送到你手上的时候，出处跟着一起走，你不用另外去翻。这一步做到，"搜一次"才从动作变成习惯。 破绽三，能做的只有一件：没数据时说没有。 AutoClaw 的位置画在这条线上：取数、整理、成稿、按时交付，这些有可校验终点的交给流程；假设成不成立、结论敢不敢署名，留给签字的人。参数和结果留下来方便复核，但留痕不是核验，核验是你签字前的最后一步。这条线具体怎么划， [AI 会取代金融分析师吗：它能写研报，但签不了字] 拆过。 工具能做到成稿，做不到签字。放到金融的日常里，AI 幻觉出现的地方很具体：季报点评、定期跟踪、同业对比，这三类活有可校验的终点——数字指得回原表、出处点得开、没数据时它说没有。终点之前的交给 AutoClaw，终点之后的交给你。三种活里，最容易被当成"随便写写"的是季报点评，最容易出事也是它，因为它看起来最像有人认真算过。 AI 幻觉识别失效的五种情况 它改写你亲手给的材料时，不灵。 数字是你喂的，出处是你给的，三个破绽一个都不会出现。这时候要核对的是它有没有改错你的数字，那是另一套防法。 逻辑层面的错，不灵。 每一步都对、结论不成立，把同时发生当成因为所以，这是判断问题，不是痕迹问题，只能靠你的专业。 源头数据本身就错，不灵。 上游数据有误，它照实引用，错得"有据可查"，三个破绽全部失效。 前三条是它管不到的。下面两条不一样，那不是管不到，是用反了。 用另一个 AI 来检测，别。 检测器自己也是模型，同样会编。开头那个自称准确率 99.8% 的工具就是证据：它用来证明自己可靠的数字，恰恰符合本文教你的第一个破绽。我后来没点进去。真要用检测器，看三件事：样本量、测试集是什么内容、方法是否公开。三个都没有，那个数字按不存在处理。 接了检索，不等于不编。 检索能压住一部分凭空生成，压不住"取回来了但读错""引用了但张冠李戴"。上面那份实测测的正是带检索的产品。 AI blogs.content: What's New Week 34 · August 17–21, 2026 Copy page Copy page Draft editable UI artboards with the /design skill, set the Concise output style, and start a Claude Code session on your machine from your phone. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.234 → v2.1.239 3 features · August 17–21 /design research preview The /design skill brings Claude Design’s artboard workflow into the CLI and Claude Code Desktop, built on artifacts. Run it with a brief and Claude publishes a canvas of editable artboards for your UI. Pick one, tweak it, then have Claude implement it. Available on Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise. Requires v2.1.234 or later. Describe what you want designed and let Claude draft the options: Claude Code > /design redesign the composer based on what people actually use it for Claude prints a link to the published canvas. Open it, pick an artboard, and tell Claude which option to implement. Where artifacts are available Concise output style v2.1.237 Concise is a new built-in output style. Claude leads with the result and skips preamble and narration, while doing the work as thoroughly as in the Default style. When you ask for an explanation or more detail, Claude answers in full. Error reports, security warnings, and confirmations for destructive actions keep their complete content. Turn it on under Output style in /config , or set it in your settings file: ~/.claude/settings.json { "outputStyle" : "Concise" } Run /clear or start a new session, and Claude’s replies lead with the result. Built-in output styles Start a session on your machine from your phone mobile Any machine running claude remote-control now shows up as a device card at the top of the Code tab in the Claude app. Remote Control is also out of research preview. Start Remote Control on the machine you want to reach, then open the Code tab on your phone: terminal claude remote-control Your machine appears as a device card at the top of the Code tab. Tap it to pick a directory and start a session there. Start a Remote Control session Other wins Claude Code now continues your session automatically when a claude.ai usage limit resets; turn it off from the Continue automatically at usage limit row in /config The optional spellcheck setting underlines misspelled words in the prompt input as you type, using your installed aspell , hunspell , or ispell On a branch with an open GitLab merge request, with the glab CLI authenticated through glab auth login , the footer shows an MR !N badge colored by whether the merge request is a draft, open, or mergeable Change the effort level from your phone or claude.ai/code and it applies to the session on your machine ; Remote Control sessions hosted by Desktop or VS Code also show connected devices the session’s current permission mode You can open /permissions or run /add-dir <path> while Claude is working; permission rule changes apply to the rest of the current turn When background tasks keep a /goal waiting, Claude checks in on them after 30 minutes instead of waiting indefinitely and keeps checking in, at longer intervals while the session sits idle; set CLAUDE_CODE_GOAL_CHECKIN_MINUTES=0 to opt out Your own prompts now render markdown in the transcript, with highlighted code blocks, inline code, and lists, the same way replies do The new ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_MODEL environment variable sets the model new sessions start on; a /model pick still overrides it and persists across restarts With the notify_when_idle input on SendMessage , Claude can ask another Claude Code session on the same machine to send one notice when it next goes idle Set keybindingFlavor to “readline” to make Ctrl+W in the prompt delete back to the previous whitespace, as Bash does, instead of stopping at punctuation such as / On native Windows, your Claude Code sessions can now message each other with SendMessage and find each other with ListAgents , as on macOS and Linux Self-hosted runners accept --defer-shutdown-max-min , which keeps serving attached sessions for

blogs.title: Week 33 · August 10–14, 2026 - Claude Code Docs
blogs.description: Claude Code Desktop auto-continues after a usage limit resets, fork mode turns on by default, and GitLab merge requests and marketplaces join GitHub.
blogs.content: What's New Week 33 · August 10–14, 2026 Copy page Copy page Claude Code Desktop auto-continues after a usage limit resets, fork mode turns on by default, and GitLab merge requests and marketplaces join GitHub. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.225 → v2.1.233 3 features · August 10–14 Auto-continue after a usage limit on Desktop Desktop When you hit your session limit in the Code tab of Claude Code Desktop, the limit card now offers an Auto-continue when limits reset checkbox. Check it, and the Desktop app retries the interrupted turn after the reset. The card shows the retry time. The weekly-limit card doesn’t offer it. The next time a session-limit card appears, check Auto-continue when limits reset and leave the session open. The card shows Auto-resuming at followed by the reset time, and the turn picks up on its own once the limit resets. What to do when you hit a usage limit Fork mode on by default v2.1.232 Fork mode is now on by default in interactive sessions. Claude can request the fork subagent type, which inherits the full conversation and prompt cache instead of starting fresh, so you don’t have to re-explain the context for a side task. Subagents Claude spawns in interactive sessions, apart from the ones an agent-team teammate spawns, also run in the background by default. Start a fork yourself with a task that needs everything you’ve discussed so far: Claude Code > /subtask draft unit tests for the parser changes so far The fork appears in the panel below your prompt and its result arrives in your conversation when it finishes. To turn fork mode off, set CLAUDE_CODE_FORK_SUBAGENT=0 . Turn fork mode on or off GitLab merge requests and marketplaces v2.1.232 Plugin marketplaces clone bare gitlab.com URLs, including nested subgroups. On v2.1.233 or later, pass a GitLab merge request URL to --worktree to branch from it, and the claude agents view labels sessions linked to a merge request as !N . Claude Code also redacts GitLab token families such as glpat- and glrt- , and protects the glab CLI’s config store the same way it protects gh . Start a session in a worktree branched from a merge request: terminal claude --worktree https://gitlab.com/group/project/-/merge_requests/42 When origin is on gitlab.com, Claude Code fetches merge-requests/42/head and opens the session on that branch in its own worktree. Branch a worktree from a pull or merge request Other wins Type @ in the prompt to mention another Claude session by name, and Claude messages it directly with SendMessage ; a bare name that matches exactly one live session now delivers without a confirmation step Interactive sessions on one machine keep unique names : if you start or rename a session with a name another live session already uses, Claude Code gives yours a name-word-word variant and tells you Plugin marketplaces accept command sources : a local command prints the plugin directory, which Claude Code re-resolves each session and applies without a restart On Linux and WSL, set CLAUDE_CODE_TOOL_MEMORY_LIMIT to a size such as 4G to cap the memory Bash and PowerShell tool commands can use The task-tracking tools, such as TaskCreate , TaskUpdate , and TodoWrite , are no longer available on Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, Mythos 5, and later models in those families ; set CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TODO_TOOLS=1 to re-enable them /code-review at high, xhigh, and max effort now runs in a background agent like the other levels /plugin install plugin@marketplace refreshes the marketplace first, so newly published plugins install without a manual marketplace update Settings accept additionalMarketplaces and allowedMarketplaces as aliases for extraKnownMarketplaces and strictKnownMarketplaces On newer models, Claude can overwrite an existing file with the Write tool without reading it first this session, matching the Edit tool’s rules; older models require the read The VS Code extension can organize the sessions list into groups : right-click to create, rename, or delete a group

blogs.name: Claude Code Releases
blogs.title: v2.1.318
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added a record of your answer when Claude Code asks to turn on the mods it writes in a session
  • Added assume_role on mantle upstreams of the Claude apps gateway, for a role in another AWS account and for per-developer AWS cost attribution
  • Added an effort option to a mod's $.model.fork, so a quick side job can run at low whatever effort the session uses; the result reports the effort sent
  • Added the date a stored claude.ai sign-in ends to claude auth status (loginExpiresAt) and to claude -p JSON results (credential_expires_at)
  • Added a one-line stderr warning to claude -p text output, starting 10 days before a stored claude.ai sign-in ends
  • Fixed --continue sometimes losing the earlier conversation after a malformed tool call's retries ran out (regression in 2.1.314)
  • Fixed macOS sessions with many running Bash commands stalling while memory grew
  • Fixed permission prompts being answered by keys typed just after sending a message, or before a slow prompt appeared
  • Fixed /logout, claude auth logout and claude mcp remove reporting success, and changes to trust, consent or MCP settings being dropped with no word, when the config file could not be updated on a shared network home directory
  • Fixed jobs exiting with Not logged in when another terminal or host signs in again to the same account and organization on the same home
  • Fixed claude mcp add and remove writing the config without its lock: they now wait for it or exit 1, though another job's save can still replace a saved server
  • Fixed claude plugin commands exiting before a slow token refresh was saved, which could sign you out on the next run
  • Fixed claude plugin validate passing a custom-named marketplace file that claude plugin marketplace add rejects
  • Fixed stdio MCP servers that exit on the version probe being re-probed on every start; a server that dies in under 3s for its own reason is also pinned to the legacy handshake for 7 days
  • Fixed sessions being refused at startup by an allowedProviders list that another login on the same machine had stored
  • Fixed idle compaction replacing a conversation with a reply that was not a summary
  • Fixed the "Now using usage credits" notice reappearing about every 30 seconds while a background subagent is running
  • Fixed custom slash commands that fail, or that only Claude can invoke, printing nothing in claude -p and SDK sessions
  • Fixed claude -p and Agent SDK sessions reporting success when an API error cut off a reply while a mod hooked turn.step
  • Fixed a message sent right after a model change still running after Stop in headless sessions: Stop now cancels or stops it as it would a queued message
  • Fixed a deleted session transcript being re-created with its last prompt when an idle non-interactive session exited
  • Fixed claude remote-control hosts, the background daemon and self-hosted runners failing to start new sessions (spawn ENOENT) after an update or version cleanup removed the binary of a still-running process
  • Fixed a running Claude Code process owned by another user (for example one left by sudo claude) being treated as dead by version cleanup, which could delete its binary
  • Fixed /remote-control showing a session as available after a failed connection
  • Fixed /design revoke reporting success when the request failed with a 404
  • Fixed a shell command approved after a self-hosted runner or cloud session restart running in the sess

blogs.name: Claude Code Releases
blogs.title: v2.1.317
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added a warning to /schedule when a new cloud scheduled task gets connectors you did not ask for, with how to remove them
  • Added a check that asks before a web or shell tool call sends your account email address to the network
  • Added onFailure: "block" for Agent SDK hook callbacks, so a callback that fails blocks the action instead of letting it run
  • Added a notice in Claude Desktop's Code tab when your organization's remote managed settings haven't loaded for the session, and another once they do
  • Added a notice when auto mode's check has no answer for a subagent's tool call, which used to leave nothing in the main view
  • Added anthropic.plan, anthropic.seat_type, anthropic.provider and anthropic.custom_base_url to OTel metrics, events and spans
  • Added a cost report to the Claude apps gateway admin API, GET /v1/organizations/analytics/cost, for reading past spend over a date range in total, per developer, per day or per IdP group
  • Added a daily record of each developer's IdP groups on Claude apps gateways with admin: set, kept for admin.identity_retention_days, which the cost report groups by
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NESTED_SESSION_ID: set it to 1 on a self-hosted runner to have claude -p run inside a session use that session's ID and transcript, as in earlier versions
  • Fixed project and local MCP servers disconnecting after the first turn in some Claude desktop sessions
  • Fixed auto mode failing every turn when an LLM gateway set as the base URL answers 403 or 422 to its server-side safety check (a 403 with an apiKeyHelper is unchanged)
  • Fixed claude auth status exiting before a slow token refresh was saved, which could sign you out on the next run
  • Fixed a project's effortLevel setting being ignored by sessions that an app starts ahead of time and then opens in the project, such as new sessions in the desktop app's Code tab
  • Fixed claude --from-pr reporting "No conversations found" in projects with many sessions when the linked session was older than the first page
  • Fixed the second of two simultaneous permission prompts showing no file path or command on claude.ai and the mobile apps
  • Fixed Remote Control and SDK hosts offering "don't ask again" on a mod's tool calls
  • Fixed session titles being lost in cloud and SDK sessions when a new message or Stop arrived while the title was generating
  • Fixed self-paced /loop wakeups sometimes not being scheduled when Claude left a field out of its request
  • Fixed auto mode in cloud sessions stopping for approval when the Artifact tool uploaded, wrote to a database or saved a file through the outputs folder
  • Fixed skills synced from claude.ai being lost or downloaded again every ten minutes when they can't be written to disk
  • Fixed /schedule leaving a cloud scheduled task's next run time and link out of its results after creating or updating it
  • Fixed screen readers speaking a running subagent's elapsed time and token count on every change in screen reader mode
  • Fixed a region or network block (HTTP 403) being shown as a sign-in failure; the error now explains the block
  • Fixed Claude saying a working claude.ai connector needed authorization or had failed in cloud sessions when a synced plugin included the same server
  • Fixed claude -p exiting 0 when a full disk or quota lost its transcript or ~/.claude.json writes; it now prints an error and, in text and json output, exits 1. Full NFS exports may be missed
  • Fixed edits to settings files made in the first second or so after launch not taking effect until a settings file changed ag

blogs.name: Claude Code Releases
blogs.title: v2.1.316
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ULTRATHINK, which turns the ultrathink keyword off
  • Added pooled group budgets to the Claude apps gateway: one monthly budget that a group's members share, on top of each member's own limit, set with pooled_budget on the spend limits admin API
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_LOOPED_CROSS_CERT_DROP to keep system cross-certificates that certify each other in a loop, for servers whose private CA needs one
  • Added CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_EFFORT to set the effort level subagents run at when nothing else names one, instead of inheriting the session's
  • Added managed.policy_mode: layered to the Claude apps gateway: every policy that matches a developer applies, each merged over the ones listed below it, not only the first
  • Added guardrail.input_tagging on Claude apps gateway Bedrock upstreams, which wraps prompts in the input tags that an Amazon Bedrock guardrail's prompt attacks filter needs; all_messages_and_system also tags the system prompt
  • Deprecated fast mode for Opus 4.8 as of October 30, 2026; it will be removed on November 30, 2026. After removal, fast mode requests on Opus 4.8 return an error and do not fall back to standard Opus 4.8. Migrate to Opus 5.5 to keep the speedup
  • Fixed shell commands being left running on macOS and Linux when Claude Code exits by itself, for example when credentials are refused or a cloud session is archived
  • Fixed bash aliases with line breaks in their value (except in Git Bash), and functions whose names start with a dash, being garbled or lost in the Bash tool's shell
  • Fixed bash scripts started from the Bash tool stopping after their first command when SHELLOPTS is exported
  • Fixed PowerShell hooks not blocking on exit code 2 when the command begins with a type cast, param, using or an attribute
  • Fixed some network requests hanging when a compressed response was cut off or corrupted
  • Fixed sonnet, opus and haiku on Vertex AI and Amazon Bedrock showing an error mid-session instead of switching to an older model when the newest is not yet available to the account or region
  • Fixed the Claude apps gateway not checking every model a request names against availableModels, deniedModels and models; a request that names a blocked model now gets a 400 naming the field
  • Fixed claude auth login refusing to run where managed settings require a Claude apps gateway; in a terminal it now shows the gateway sign-in
  • Fixed --restricted sessions uploading files from outside the working directories when a Read allow rule covered them
  • Fixed prompts containing invisible characters needing a second Enter to send; plain prompts now send cleaned on the first Enter, and commands still wait for review
  • Fixed sub-agents that inherited a parent sub-agent's model moving to the main model when a background job or message woke them
  • Fixed a managed autoMode.allow list without "$defaults" getting the built-in exceptions back from a host app's --settings, a first rule added in /permissions, or /auto-mode-setup
  • Fixed cloud sessions and cloud scheduled tasks not being marked as failed when auto mode stopped a turn because the server returned no safety verdict
  • Fixed claude -p text output sometimes not saying why auto mode stopped a turn when a background agent was still running
  • Fixed CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=1 being ignored in sessions started by a host application (such as Claude Desktop) behind a proxy or LLM gateway with experimental betas turned off
  • Fixed plugin

blogs.name: Claude Code Releases
blogs.title: v2.1.314
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories: Write, Edit and NotebookEdit refuse paths outside the working directories in every permission mode
  • Added an optional groups list to Claude apps gateway upstreams: only developers in the listed IdP groups are sent to that upstream, on failover too
  • Added guardrail_trace to Claude apps gateway Bedrock upstreams, to log which Amazon Bedrock guardrail filter fired on a request, without the matched text
  • Added idle compaction to VS Code and Claude Desktop's Code tab: a 200K+ token conversation left idle is summarized, and the summary is used on your next message if the prompt cache has expired
  • Fixed sessions failing turn after turn with "Invalid effort level" when an organization's admin caps a model's effort: Claude Code now lowers the effort, retries, and says which level it uses
  • Fixed claude -p exiting with code 0 and no output when startup failed; it now prints the error and exits 1
  • Fixed Bedrock sessions with many images failing every turn and /compact with "400 Input is too long." instead of removing older images and compacting
  • Fixed Microsoft Foundry sessions failing when the resource has no deployment for the default Sonnet, Opus or Haiku model: Claude Code now falls back to an older model of that family
  • Fixed repeated refused requests behind a gateway that doesn't accept tool search's tool_reference blocks: the request is sent again once without tool search, and the session remembers
  • Fixed TLS connections failing with UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT when the system certificate store holds a renewed root certificate that is cross-signed with its predecessor
  • Fixed MCP servers that also work without sign-in showing "needs authentication" after their stored sign-in stopped working; they are now used signed out
  • Fixed claude mcp logout reporting success when the MCP sign-in was not removed, for example while the macOS keychain is locked over SSH
  • Fixed extra sign-in renewals when several sessions share an Anthropic profile login and the credentials lock is busy
  • Fixed claude ultrareview and claude remote-control asking the workspace trust question in a CI job that has a terminal; with CI set they now refuse an untrusted folder at once
  • Fixed an administrator's TLS trust settings in managed settings not being applied in Claude Desktop sessions
  • Fixed model switching being refused on machines with managed plugin settings when one of your own --plugin-dir or --plugin-url plugins had a broken manifest or failed to download
  • Fixed the Bedrock and Vertex model upgrade offer coming back at every start when managed settings pin the model
  • Fixed forceRemoteSettingsRefresh set only in remote managed settings no longer applying once the stored copy had expired, which let sessions start without policy when the server could not be reached
  • Fixed "Continue automatically at usage limit" continuing more than three times without a prompt from you when a task restarted itself between waits (a /goal check-in, a background or scheduled task)
  • Fixed background and cloud sessions started with Ultracode turning it back on at their next start after it had been switched off
  • Fixed the last broken reply and its retry prompts staying in the conversation after Claude gave up on a tool call that could not be parsed
  • Fixed a PreCompact hook with very large output making compaction fail or repeat; each hook's output is now cut at 10,000 characters
  • Fixed background diff refreshes briefly taking the repository's index lock, which could make a git command run at the same moment fail with "Unable to create '.git/index.lo

blogs.name: Claude Code Releases
blogs.title: v2.1.312
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added oidc.user_id_claim to the Claude apps gateway, to identify people by an id_token claim other than sub, such as Microsoft Entra ID's oid
  • Added click to send: in fullscreen, clicking the "to send now" hint under a queued message sends it right away, as its key does
  • Fixed managed settings and organization policy not being fetched for the rest of the session after signing in from the VS Code extension
  • Fixed Claude overwriting a very large CLAUDE.md, rules file or @-included file in a subdirectory after seeing only its start; Write now asks Claude to read it all or edit in place
  • Fixed per-directory and paths: skills not being found after a Bash cd deeper into a git repository
  • Fixed a rare case where the first reply after resuming a session in the terminal could be missing the next time the session was resumed
  • Fixed a command with an invalid name stopping all commands from loading, which could leave claude -p with no output
  • Fixed the Read tool sometimes failing on PDF pages with "pdftoppm failed: Could not write image" when the clean-up of old session files ran at the same time
  • Fixed the spinner, OpenTelemetry effort values and transcripts naming a newly picked effort level during a task before the model applied it; they now show the level in force
  • Fixed the /model and /effort cache warning saying the re-read waits for your next message; a change made while Claude is working can trigger it sooner
  • Fixed some sessions showing as waiting on you when the last message only mentioned items waiting on you mid-sentence
  • Fixed agent view restoring input text on the next launch after it was cleared with Ctrl+C just before exiting
  • Fixed agent view reopening in shell mode after exiting with Ctrl+D from an empty ! input
  • Fixed vim mode d, c and y with a gj or gk count larger than the lines left deleting or copying text; like Vim, they now only move the cursor
  • Fixed /verify showing a long description meant for Claude in /help and the / command menu instead of a short one
  • Improved the prompt's effort indicator: a change made mid-task now says it may wait for your next message, and the note clears when it no longer applies
  • Improved WebFetch errors in cloud sessions: a host that does not resolve is now explained as possibly outside the allowed network domains, so Claude names the host to allow
  • Changed Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry and Mantle to use the shorter system prompt for model names Claude Code doesn't recognize, such as custom deployment names and inference profile ARNs, even when they front Sonnet or Haiku; set CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE_SYSTEM_PROMPT=0 to keep the full prompt
  • Changed automatic model switches after a flagged message to also cover model names Claude Code doesn't recognize, such as custom deployment names; set CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_REFUSAL_FALLBACK=1 to turn them off
  • Changed usage limit messages to call the 5-hour window the "5-hour limit" instead of the "session limit"
  • Changed cloud sessions started from the CLI to get their names and branch names from the server
  • Changed prompt and agent hooks to run at most 24 at a time per session, sub-agents included, plus at most 12 that have waited longer than their event's timeout; a timeout under 1 second now counts as 1 second
  • Changed a subagent's autoCompactWindow to lower the window set by CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW, where it had no effect before; it still never raises that window
  • Changed OpenTelemetry mcp_server.name to report the real name of f

blogs.title: v2.1.311
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added --hold-idle-file and --max-hold-min to self-hosted-runner, to keep an idle session while your host reports processes it left running
  • Added a tip for the Explanatory output style, shown when you ask Claude for explanations
  • Fixed long freezes at startup and after reading or editing files when a CLAUDE.md file holds a very long list item
  • Fixed interrupting Claude not taking effect until a timeout while an MCP server had not answered a resource read or a skill was still downloading
  • Fixed standard-context sessions stopping with "Usage credits required for 1M context" when a request ran over 200K tokens; Claude Code now compacts the conversation and continues
  • Fixed Write and Edit stalling for up to 5 seconds after they ran, and reporting 0 lines changed, when changing thousands of lines in a file
  • Fixed subagents being unable to use MCP tools from servers that finish connecting after the subagent starts
  • Fixed Claude seeing stale MEMORY.md and CLAUDE.md content right after automatic compaction when those files were edited earlier in the session
  • Fixed claude -p and SDK sessions saving transcript messages out of order or keeping messages that were taken back
  • Fixed SubagentStop hooks running about twice a minute for each running subagent instead of once when it finishes
  • Fixed the @ file picker ignoring .ignore/.rgignore negation rules that re-include git-ignored files
  • Fixed a subagent's isolated worktree being removed while a background subagent it started was still working in it
  • Fixed background agents in auto mode that wait on their own shells starting a new main conversation turn on every wake
  • Fixed the Bash tool description claiming the working directory always persists between calls
  • Fixed the environment block naming a shell commands don't run in, such as fish when the Bash tool uses zsh
  • Fixed claude mcp add, claude mcp remove and /mcp naming the current folder instead of the project entry in ~/.claude.json that holds a local-scope server when run below a repository root
  • Fixed claude mcp list and claude mcp get showing the error code twice on failed-connection lines (for example ENOENT: ENOENT: …)
  • Fixed Remote Control sessions staying on "Connecting" for about two minutes when a network proxy blocks a startup request
  • Fixed messages that Claude sends to a cloud or Remote Control session appearing as your own message in the Claude mobile apps
  • Fixed Claude not being told the cause when a file attached to a message sent over Remote Control or to a cloud session could not be saved because the disk was full, or that a message's attachments past the first 20 were left out
  • Fixed WebFetch and WebSearch hanging on a stalled response in Cowork cloud sessions; an unfinished request now fails after 300 seconds
  • Fixed a background session that crashed between turns not being restarted while it was attached, pinned, or had a scheduled task or wake-up set
  • Fixed the "background service did not respond" error suggesting the disabled claude daemon restart; it now suggests claude daemon stop --any and says it ends background sessions
  • Fixed claude respawn starting the background service before reporting that no background session matches the id
  • Fixed /effort not warning about a prompt cache miss in plan mode when the plan model differs from the session model
  • Fixed /ide saying the VS Code extension was installed before the install finished or when it failed
  • Fixed the Write tool's file preview skipping rows and miscounting hidden lines when

blogs.name: Claude Code Releases
blogs.title: v2.1.310
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Added the Monitor tool and plugin monitors on Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry, and when telemetry or nonessential traffic is disabled; long foreground sleeps are now blocked there too
  • Fixed requests failing behind some gateways and compatible servers that reject the effort-2025-11-24 beta value or mid-conversation system messages; Claude Code now retries without them
  • Fixed background cleanup deleting some recent files, such as pasted images, when cleanupPeriodDays is set to a very large value
  • Fixed compaction after a "Prompt is too long" error keeping too much of a conversation with dense text, such as base64 or SVG, so the next request could fail again
  • Fixed file read permission prompts not showing where a symbolic link leads
  • Fixed a question's auto-continue timeout firing the moment the external editor closed after a long edit
  • Windows: Fixed PreToolUse and PermissionRequest hooks letting a tool call through when Git Bash is missing and the hook's command is only quoted strings, such as a quoted path
  • Improved auto mode's prompt before the first read outside the working directories: it now says when blocking those reads makes shell commands ask for permission
  • Improved memory use of non-interactive sessions (-p, Agent SDK) during compaction when the transcript file is very large
  • Improved a mod's Image to draw inside tmux with allow-passthrough and focus-events on, in kitty, Ghostty, and iTerm2 3.5+ with fullscreen rendering, where it showed only its alt text
  • Linux: Improved /sandbox and the sandbox startup warning to name Ubuntu's AppArmor restriction on user namespaces, and how to lift it, when it keeps bubblewrap from starting the sandbox
  • Changed the error for an MCP tool call that times out in a non-interactive session while the server's elicitation is unanswered: it now tells Claude that no answer came and not to repeat the call
  • [VSCode] Fixed pressing Enter on the plan review card's "Send feedback and keep planning" button approving the plan instead of sending your comments back
  • [VSCode] Fixed the panel showing "Something went wrong" after "Switch branch & continue" on a cloud session opened from Session history's Web tab
  • [Cloud sessions] Added Claude Code cloud sessions and Remote Control permissions to Enterprise custom roles, so Owners can control access to each by role
  • [Cloud sessions] Added a Choose file button to load a cloud environment's setup script from a file
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed failed saves and archives in the cloud environment edit dialog showing no error inside the dialog
  • [Cloud sessions] Fixed failed routine API token actions showing only a toast; the error now appears in the routine edit dialog
  • [Cloud sessions] Improved the session start checklist to show a cloud environment's setup script output in a scrolling box
  • [Cloud sessions] Changed turning on Cloud sessions or Remote Control in admin settings to ask for confirmation and list the custom roles that have that permission
  • [Cloud sessions] Changed the cloud environment dialog to open network access, setup script and environment variables from rows instead of listing every editor at once
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag treating ! commands such as !restart and !help as ordinary messages when sent in bold, italic or strikethrough
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag admin channel and workspace pages being replaced by a load error when a background refresh of the bundle list fails
  • [Claude Tag] Fixed Claude Tag's spend limits page in admin settings reporting that no channels match a filter while channel names are still loading
  • [Code Review] Fixed the Code Review admin section hidi

blogs.name: Claude Code Releases
blogs.title: v2.1.309
blogs.author: ashwin-ant
blogs.content:
What's changed

  • Fixed sandboxed Bash commands on macOS and Linux running the shell's startup files outside the sandbox before each command
  • Fixed macOS sandbox denyWrite glob patterns not applying at a path's real location when the pattern's folder is reached through a symlink
  • Fixed sandboxed commands and auto-accepted edits being able to modify the MCP config file passed with --mcp-config
  • Fixed a disabled MCP server being reconnected by a later permission prompt in print and SDK sessions
  • Fixed the Bash permission check trusting a variable set by a command whose redirect can fail to open
  • Fixed Bash permission checks not prompting for some compound commands that change directory before running git when the cd is wrapped or prefixed, as they do for a plain cd
  • Fixed an Edit(path) deny rule not blocking a Bash redirect to that path in some commands that also held a subshell
  • Fixed worktree-isolated sessions accepting some locale-prefixed commands the isolation guard should refuse
  • Fixed worktree-isolated sessions on zsh accepting some arithmetic commands that the isolation guard should refuse
  • Fixed worktrees and branch checkouts that Claude Code creates so they ignore git replace refs, as its other git operations already do
  • Fixed profile store write protection not applying when the config directory is reached through a symlink
  • Fixed sessions compacting repeatedly after reading files under a very large nested CLAUDE.md; a nested CLAUDE.md over the size limit now loads only its start
  • Fixed ctrl+enter (send now) only queuing a message when pressed before the response had started, and restarting a prompt's hooks while leaving the message queued when pressed while those hooks were running
  • Fixed key-bound slash commands running in the shell from ! mode
  • Fixed ctrl+o not showing messages from other agents and sessions that are still waiting to be delivered; they now appear in full under the transcript, marked as waiting
  • Fixed long tool output previews being cut through an emoji, leaving session transcripts that jq could not parse
  • Fixed Read reporting "File does not exist" for PDF page ranges in Linux sandboxes that share the parent's /proc
  • Fixed messages from a Claude Desktop-hosted session sometimes being lost when its connection refreshed
  • Fixed features missing from Claude Code sessions in the Claude desktop app when the terminal on the same computer was signed in to a different account or organization
  • Fixed the claude remote-control status line showing HEAD as the branch for a folder that is not in a git repository
  • Fixed split-pane agent teammates not inheriting the tool deny and --tools rules given on the leader's command line
  • Fixed sessions renamed with /rename appearing to other sessions under a generated name after a VS Code window reload or a non-interactive --resume
  • Fixed the /rewind list showing "No code changes" for a turn that changed checkpointed files through /code-review --fix, a subagent or a shell command
  • Fixed /privacy-settings showing an out-of-date "Help improve our AI models" value; it now also says when the setting can't be fetched
  • Fixed feedback saying "try again later" when your organization does not accept feedback; it now shows the server's reason and where to report a bug
  • Fixed oversized /feedback reports failing instead of being resent without the transcript

What's changed

  • Fixed requests failing with a model-not-found error when CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_1M_CONTEXT is set and the model is an alias with the [1m] suffix, such as opus[1m]
  • Fixed the prompt-caching-scope beta header being sent behind custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL gateways and on Foundry, where it has no effect
  • Fixed MCP servers showing "needs authentication" in claude -p on macOS while the login keychain was locked; they now say why, and the next run after an unlock connects without a new sign-in
  • Fixed MCP servers being reported as timed out, and staying failed in headless runs, when a macOS or Linux computer went to sleep while they were connecting
  • Fixed HTTP MCP tool calls being sent twice when the connection closed mid-call; only read-only or idempotent tools are now retried
  • Fixed a turn sometimes starting without an SDK MCP server's latest tools when a background task was running
  • Fixed some "Autocompact is thrashing" errors in turns that read many PDF pages, images or other large tool results
  • Fixed /autocompact in cloud sessions going back to the default window after the session restarted
  • Fixed a conversation cleared with /clear sometimes coming back when a cloud or self-hosted runner session restarted
  • Fixed CLAUDE_STREAM_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS being ignored in Claude apps gateway sessions
  • Fixed telemetry from Claude Desktop sessions behind a Claude apps gateway being rejected when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS is set
  • Fixed /permissions > Recently denied not showing the denied shell command, and auto mode's local classifier ignoring an approval from there when it checks a retried command; approving a row now names the command, not its description
  • Fixed /help and the / command menu showing long model-facing descriptions for bundled skills such as /claude-api instead of their short descriptions
  • Fixed subagent transcripts recording placeholder token usage and an empty stop reason for streamed responses
  • Fixed model switches through the Agent SDK's setModel(), and apps built on it, being refused when the API took more than 5 seconds to confirm the model; Claude Code now waits up to 15 seconds
  • Fixed a background command stopped through a connected app (such as the desktop app archiving an idle session) being reported to Claude as stopped by the user; the notice now names its output file
  • Fixed WebFetch in Cowork cloud sessions reporting a tool error when a site answered with a 4xx status or a robots.txt refusal; it is now a normal result, as in local sessions
  • Fixed write tools on a directly configured GitHub MCP server showing a form that closed without creating anything in the desktop app's Code tab
  • Fixed Artifact tool reads failing with a connection reset when the server had closed a reused connection
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed sessions with --use-anthropic-git-proxy committing a .claude/settings.local.json left in the clone by an earlier session
  • Self-hosted runner: Fixed archiving or requeueing a session, or stopping the runner, during its checkout hook leaving the hook's processes running and the runner's slot held
  • Improved recovery from unparseable tool calls: Claude Code now retries the call up to twice before ending the turn with an error
  • Improved fork subagents launched together: each is now told

blogs.description: Claude Code sessions message each other, self-hosted environments run cloud sessions on your infrastructure, and auto mode becomes the default permission mode.
blogs.content: What's New Week 32 · August 3–7, 2026 Copy page Copy page Claude Code sessions message each other, self-hosted environments run cloud sessions on your infrastructure, and auto mode becomes the default permission mode. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.220 → v2.1.224 3 features · August 3–7 Cross-session messaging v2.1.224 Your Claude Code sessions can now message each other. Claude discovers your other sessions with the ListAgents tool and sends with SendMessage , either when you ask it to or on its own, such as after a change in one session affects what another is working on. A message is text Claude writes for the other session, never your conversation history or files. Available on macOS and Linux. Requires v2.1.224 or later. With two sessions open on the same machine, ask one of them to pass something along: Claude Code Tell the session working on the payments API that users.name is now users.display_name The other session shows a Message from row once Claude has read the message; press Ctrl+O to expand it. To see which sessions Claude can reach, run /list-agents . Message another session Self-hosted environments v2.1.224 Self-hosted environments run Claude Code cloud sessions on your organization’s own infrastructure, in public beta on Team and Enterprise plans. Run claude self-hosted-runner on your machines or containers to turn them into runners. When someone picks your environment while starting a session from claude.ai, the mobile or desktop apps, or claude --cloud , that session runs inside your network, with access to your internal services. An Owner turns on Allow self-hosted environments in admin settings first. Signed in as an Owner, run the guided setup, which walks you through creating the environment and starts a runner: terminal claude self-hosted-runner setup The environment shows Healthy in admin settings once the runner registers. Self-hosted environments quickstart Auto mode becomes the default CLI Starting August 14, auto mode is the default permission mode for new sessions on Pro, Max, and Team plans. If you set a default mode yourself, it stays in place unless you accept the one-time switch prompt, and a default your organization manages doesn’t change. You can still switch modes at any time. Already in effect on those plans: the classifier calls auto mode makes no longer count toward your usage limits. To start every session in auto mode before the switch, set it as your default in your user settings: ~/.claude/settings.json { "permissions" : { "defaultMode" : "auto" } } New sessions then show auto mode on in the status bar. Auto mode requirements and controls Other wins The VS Code extension gets Focus view , which hides tool activity behind one expandable row per turn; toggle it from the command menu or with Ctrl+Alt+F ( Ctrl+Option+F on Mac) Sandbox credential files accept mode: “mask” on Linux and WSL2, so sandboxed commands read a sentinel copy while the sandbox proxy substitutes the real value on egress; credential masking also gains extract , JWT-aware decode , and AWS SigV4 re-signing options Marketplaces can distribute a plugin as a zip archive with the new archive source, downloaded over HTTPS with an optional SHA-256 pin, so installs work without git or npm /review is now an alias of /code-review , and /code-review with no effort level reuses the level you typed last A session you copy with /fork now makes its code changes in a worktree of its own instead of the original session’s checkout Plugins you install from /plugin activate in the current session when it’s safe to do so; the install summary reports Plugin is now active. or tells you to run /reload-plugins Background sessions that changed code in a worktree now commit and push before finishing, open a draft pull request only when the task calls for one, and follow the git instructions in your CLAUDE.md The 200-subagent-per-session cap is removed, so long-running sessions no longer refuse new subagents; the concurrency and depth limits

blogs.title: AI 调研结果可靠吗？用 5 道检查核验来源、数据和结论
blogs.author: AutoClaw Team
blogs.description: AI 竞品分析怎么做、AI Agent 适合做什么、如何评估 AI Agent
blogs.content: 返回博客 AI 调研结果可靠吗？用 5 道检查核验来源、数据和结论 教程 作者：AutoClaw Team 2026年11月2日 AI 竞品分析怎么做、AI Agent 适合做什么、如何评估 AI Agent AI 调研结果可以使用，但不能因为文章写得完整、表格整齐、引用很多，就默认它可靠。判断可靠性要看五件事：研究边界是否清楚，来源是否可打开，原文是否支持对应主张，数据口径是否一致，结论是否超出证据。只要其中一道检查没有通过，调研报告就应该保留“待确认”，而不是补一句更肯定的表达。 可靠性不是一个分数，而是一条证据链 一份调研报告通常包含三层内容：原始事实、整理或计算结果、作者判断。例如，价格页写明“每月 100 元”是事实；换算为年支出是计算；“更适合 20 人团队”则是带条件的判断。如果这三层混在一起，即使原始数字没有错，最后的建议也可能不可信。 内容类型 应该保留什么 常见问题 事实 原始页面、引用位置、访问日期 二手文章被当作官方说明 计算 输入数据、单位、公式、取整规则 每月与每年、分钟与小时混用 判断 适用条件、前提、反例和不确定性 把局部优势写成绝对排名 第一道检查：研究问题和截止日期是否清楚 调研报告必须先回答“为谁做什么决策”。“研究 AI 办公软件”范围太宽；“为 20 人的中文内容团队选择一款支持会议转写、纪要和待办导出的工具”才是可以验证的问题。 对价格、产品功能、政策和市场数据，还要保留截止日期或访问日期。没有时间边界的调研，可能在写完时已经过期，却无法判断哪一条需要重新查证。 第二道检查：来源等级是否匹配结论 来源不是越多越好，而是要匹配要证明的内容。价格应优先查价格页或购买页，权限与数据处理应查帮助中心、用户协议和隐私文本，已上线功能应查官方文档或实际产品页。搜索摘要、媒体转述和论坛评论可以帮助发现线索，但不应单独支撑价格、安全或权限结论。 如果官方页面没有说明，应该写“未找到官方说明”，而不是直接写“不支持”。前者是对本次检索结果的描述，后者是对产品能力的判定，两者的证据要求不同。 第三道检查：每条引用是否真的支持对应主张 引用链接能打开，不代表引用正确。复核时要逐条回到原页面，查看它是否真的包含报告中的数字、限制条件和时间范围。有时页面确实提到了某个功能，但只适用于特定套餐、地区或测试阶段；如果报告删掉这些条件，结论就会扩大。 建议把报告中每一项具体主张拆成一行证据表，至少保留：主张、原文摘要、来源类型、页面地址、访问日期、是否支持、待确认项。这张表比报告末尾的“参考资料列表”更容易发现错引。 第四道检查：数据口径和计算是否一致 数字的问题往往不是“算错”，而是比较了不同口径。免费额度可能按人、企业、月或年计算；时长可能使用分钟、小时或次数；用户规模可能指注册、活跃、付费或企业客户。不先统一定义，就不能直接放进同一张对比表。 所有二次计算都应保留输入值、公式和单位。如果结果来自推算，就明确标记为“推算”，不要伪装成原始来源直接公布的数据。遇到同一产品的不同官方页面数值冲突时，不要自行选一个“看起来更合理”的数字，应并列记录并标为待确认。 第五道检查：结论是否超出证据 调研的最后一道门不是增加修饰，而是删掉过度推断。“官方页面显示支持某项功能”不等于“所有用户都能使用”；“样本中 60% 的公司提到某能力”不等于“全行业 60% 的岗位都需要它”。 一个可靠的结论应该同时写出适用对象、前提、例外和未验证项。如果最终要做采购、投资、医疗、法律或安全决策，AI 报告只能作为前期资料，关键数据、合同条款和专业判断必须由对应负责人确认。 用 AutoClaw 把“生成报告”拆成“生成 + 复核” 与其只对 AutoClaw 说“帮我做一份准确的调研报告”，不如把任务分成两轮。第一轮负责搜集、结构化和成稿；第二轮专门重新打开每个来源，检查页面是否有效、是否支持对应主张，并保留修改记录。 AutoClaw 官网已公开的 AI 竞品分析案例中，任务最终保留了 58 条官方一手来源，并在复核阶段记录官方页面之间的口径冲突。这个案例的价值不在于“引用多”，而在于报告、来源表、访问日期和修改记录可以互相追溯。 可直接复用的两轮任务 第一轮：请围绕我的决策问题完成调研。优先使用官网、官方帮助文档、价格页、公告和正式条款。为每条具体信息记录来源地址、来源类型、访问日期和原文支持内容。找不到官方依据时写“未找到官方说明”，不要用常识补齐。交付调研报告和来源表，报告中分开标注事实、计算、判断和待确认项。 第二轮：请逐条复核来源表。重新打开每个页面，检查链接是否有效、页面是否支持对应主张、数字和限制条件是否与当前页面一致。对失效、不支持或口径冲突的条目进行修正，无法确认的标为待确认。在报告末尾增加复核修改记录，写明改了什么、为什么改。 三分钟检查一份 AI 调研报告 标题或开头是否写明研究对象、范围和截止日期 关键数字是否能回到具体原始页面 价格、权限和安全主张是否优先使用正式来源 计算是否保留单位、公式和输入值 报告是否区分事实、推算、判断和待确认 结论是否写出适用条件，而不是只给绝对排名 来源表是否经过第二轮重新打开和修正 常见问题 AI 调研结果可靠吗？ 在研究问题清楚、来源可追溯、数据口径统一、引用经过二次复核、结论没有超出证据时，AI 调研可以作为有效的决策辅助。如果报告只有流畅文字而没有证据表和复核记录，不应直接用于重要决策。 引用很多就代表可靠吗？ 不代表。引用的价值在于能否准确支持对应主张，而不是数量。十个无关或二手来源，不如一个直接支持数据的正式页面。 AI 写调研报告最容易错在哪里？ 常见错误包括研究问题过宽、把搜索摘要当原文、不同数据口径直接对比、引用没有访问日期、把“未找到”写成“不支持”，以及只做第一轮汇总而没有逐条复核。 结论 AI 调研的优势是快速搜集、结构化整理和形成初稿，但“写得快”不等于“结论可信”。把一次生成拆成资料搜集和二次复核，要求 AutoClaw 同时交付报告、来源表和修改记录，再由人确认口径、冲突与最终判断，才能让调研结果真正可追溯、可复查、可用于决策。

blogs.description: Opus 5 becomes the default Opus model, Claude Code Desktop adds an iOS Simulator pane, and the Claude Security plugin scans your code for vulnerabilities.
blogs.content: What's New Week 30 · July 20–24, 2026 Copy page Copy page Opus 5 becomes the default Opus model, Claude Code Desktop adds an iOS Simulator pane, and the Claude Security plugin scans your code for vulnerabilities. Copy page Copy page Releases v2.1.214 → v2.1.219 3 features · July 20–24 Claude Opus 5 new model Claude Opus 5 is the new default Opus model in Claude Code. It’s the default on Max, Team Premium, Enterprise pay-as-you-go, and the Anthropic API, and on Claude Platform on AWS, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud’s Agent Platform. On the Anthropic API and on Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, Opus 5 runs with a 1M-token context window ; on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud’s Agent Platform, select the 1M model variant. Fast mode moves to Opus 5 at $10/$50 per MTok. Requires v2.1.219 or later. Switch to Opus 5 by name, or pick it from the model picker: Claude Code > /model claude-opus-5 Model configuration iOS Simulator in Claude Code Desktop Desktop Claude Code Desktop on macOS gets an iOS Simulator pane, in public beta on Pro, Max, and Team plans. When Claude builds, launches, or checks your app in a simulator, the pane opens next to the conversation and streams the device screen live, so you can watch Claude tap through the app to verify its changes or drive the device yourself. Requires Xcode with the iOS platform installed, and Claude Desktop v1.24012.0 or later. Ask Claude to run or test your app, and the pane opens when the app launches: Claude Code > Build the app and run it in the simulator to check the onboarding flow. Test iOS apps in the simulator Claude Security plugin plugin The Claude Security plugin runs a multi-agent vulnerability scan of your codebase inside a Claude Code session: agents map your architecture, build a threat model, hunt for vulnerabilities, and independently review every finding before writing the report to a CLAUDE-SECURITY-<timestamp>/ directory. Scan a whole repository or only a branch’s diff, a pull request, or a single commit, then turn the findings you choose into reviewed patches that you apply yourself. Install the plugin from the official Anthropic marketplace, run /reload-plugins , then start a scan with /claude-security : Claude Code > /plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official Scan and fix your codebase Other wins /code-review now runs as a background subagent with its own context window, so review work stays out of your conversation and the findings arrive when it completes /verify , /code-review , and /deep-research run only when you invoke them; Claude no longer launches them on its own Emoji shortcodes autocomplete in the prompt input: type :heart: to insert an emoji, or two or more characters after : for suggestions; turn it off with emojiCompletionEnabled Skills with context: fork run in the background by default, and background: false in the skill’s frontmatter waits for the result in the same turn A session runs up to 20 subagents concurrently by default; change the limit with CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS --max-budget-usd now enforces the cap on subagents: once spend reaches it, Claude can’t start more and running background subagents stop New sandbox.filesystem.disabled setting skips filesystem isolation while keeping network egress control In auto mode, the checks for dangerous rm commands, background jobs, and suspicious Windows paths no longer open permission dialogs; the auto-mode classifier adjudicates them instead Bash permission checks fail closed on more shell forms, including file-descriptor redirects, Zsh variable subscripts in [[ ]] comparisons, help and man invocations that could run unsafe options, and commands over 10,000 characters Fast mode no longer supports Opus 4.7: /fast now applies to Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 Long-running tool calls emit a periodic progress heartbeat instead of going silent Full changelog for v2.1.214–v2.1.219 → Was this page helpful? use /ide from an outside terminal or your editor’s extensions view Changed subagents to stop instead of switching models when “Switch models when a message is flagged” is set to “Ask each time” Changed background subagents to move a shell command to the background after 3 minutes on all providers, so the prompt cache doesn’t expire while it runs Changed subagent progress summaries on Bedrock, Vertex, Foundry, or with telemetry off: on a cold prompt cache, one can now wait up to 5 minutes for the subagent’s pending response Changed what a mod attaches at prompt.submit to stay in the user’s turn rather than go out as a system message Changed deniedMcpServers URL entries to also block Anthropic-provided servers whose upstream URL matches, and connectors in cloud sessions and on self-hosted runners, where the session is given the connector’s own URL;
